Subject: Interruption on dedicated pool (Aug 6) — request for compensation

Hi Marcus,

We observed degraded availability for our dedicated pool on Aug 6 between ~02:10 and 04:40 PDT. Our monitoring shows effective uptime of ~99.20% for that UTC day versus the 99.95% SLA in our agreement. This affected two production services and caused throttling and retries; attached is the export of our telemetry for the window (novus_incident_export_aug6.json).

Can you confirm Redwood's timeline and whether this qualifies for an SLA credit? Please advise next steps: what info you need and an expected cadence for calculation and issuance. We would like the credit applied to the Aug invoice if eligible.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Park
VP, Cloud Operations | NovusCloud

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: marcus.lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@novuscloud.io>
Date: 2026-08-12T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: INF-2239 — incident timeline and preliminary SLA calculation

Folks —

We completed the post-incident review for the Aug 6 dedicated-pool degradation. Summary:
- Incident window: 2026-08-06T02:10:00Z - 2026-08-06T04:40:00Z (approx. 2h30m)
- Root cause: rolling kernel upgrade on underlying host cluster triggered KV-cache warm-up and request queuing on two shards; autoscaling did not fully compensate during the early warm-up period.
- Impact: region-us dedicated pool experienced sustained degraded responsiveness and partial request failures for affected shard set.

SLA rules applied:
- Contracted availability: 99.95% (monthly window)
- Observed availability for the affected day: 99.20% (per customer's telemetry and our cross-check)

Preliminary calculation (per SLA section 4.2):
- Monthly committed fee (reported by customer): $45,000
- SLA shortfall = 99.95% - 99.20% = 0.75% of the monthly window
- Credit = monthly committed fee * SLA shortfall = $45,000 * 0.0075 = $337.50

Attachments: novus_sla_calc_aug2026.xlsx (spreadsheet with timestamped calculation and exported log ranges).

Notes/edges: we excluded a 10-minute maintenance window where scheduled patching occurred under the maintenance SLA carve-out. The 2h30m above is after exclusions and matches NovusCloud's telemetry.

Proposed next step: Finance approval to issue the credit as an invoice adjustment for the Aug billing cycle. If approved, we will add a line item "SLA credit — Aug 6 incident (INF-2239)" referencing invoice INV-7890.

Hannah Schmitt
SRE — Redwood Inference

Thanks — Kimberly
